PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Respondent(s) No. 1 RULE SERVED BY DS for the Respondent(s) No. 2 ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE DIVYESH A. JOSHI  Date : 16/02/2024
ORAL ORDER 1.

The present application is filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for regular bail in connection with the FIR being C.R. No.11207078230168 of 2023 registered with the Kakanpur Police Station, Panchmahals of the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366 &
376(2)(j) of the IPC and Sections 4, 6 and 12 of the POCSO Act.
2. Learned advocate appearing for the applicant has submitted that the applicant-accused was arrested on 26.05.2023 and since then he is in jail.
Learned advocate for the applicant has also submitted that the investigation has already been completed and charge-sheet has also been filed.

Learned advocate for the applicant has submitted that it is a case of love affair and the victim girl, on her free will and volition, left her parental home an eloped with the applicant- accused which is evident from her statement recorded by the police during the course of investigation.

It is moreso submitted that the deposition of the victim girl has also been NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/16316/2023 ORDER DATED: 16/02/2024 undefined recorded during the course of trial,
wherein she has not supported the case of the prosecution and turned hostile.

It is submitted that Vishalkumar Santoshbhai Vasava vs State Of Gujarat on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30421194/
1 the applicant-accused is a young boy aged about 21 years.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Under the circumstances, learned advocate for the applicant prays that the applicant may be enlarged on bail on any suitable terms and conditions.
3. The learned APP appearing on behalf of the respondent- State has opposed grant of regular bail looking to the nature and gravity of the offence.

Learned APP has submitted that considering the role attributed to the applicant-accused, this is a fit case wherein discretionary power of this Court is not required to be exercised in favour of the applicant-accused.
4. Though served, none appears on behalf of the original complainant either in person or through an advocate and oppose the present bail application.
5. The learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties do not press for further reasoned order.

6. I have heard the learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties and perused the papers of the investigation and considered the allegations levelled against the applicant and the role played by the applicant.

This Court has also taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation, reported in [2012]1 SCC 40.
8.

entities.text: Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation, reported in [2012]1 SCC 40
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the nature of the allegations made against the applicant in the FIR, without discussing the evidence in detail, prima facie, this Court is of the opinion that this is a fit case to exercise the discretion and enlarge the applicant on regular bail.

sentences.text: The authorities will release the applicant only if he is not required in connection with any other offence for the time being.
If breach of any of the above conditions is committed, the Sessions Judge concerned will be free to issue warrant or take appropriate action in the matter.
11. Bail bond to be executed before the lower Court having jurisdiction to try the case.
It will be open for the concerned Court to delete, modify and/or relax any of the above conditions, in accordance with law.
12. At the trial, the trial Court shall not be influenced by the observations of preliminary nature qua the evidence at this stage made by this Court while enlarging the applicant on bail.
Direct service is permitted.
